name: BlogHub
projectType: Full-stack web application (monetized multi-vendor blogging platform)
description: BlogHub is a multi-vendor blogging platform where creators sign up, publish articles, and earn money from the engagement their content receives, while administrators manage users, categories, earning rules and payouts. Visitors can read articles and interact through likes, comments, shares and views. The backend is an Express application that mounts separate route groups for normal users and for admins, with JWT-based authentication protecting private routes. Content, engagement and money data are stored in MongoDB collections, and an AI-assisted moderation step reviews submitted articles before they reach readers. The project demonstrates how a real content business is structured: publishing, engagement tracking, creator earnings, withdrawals and administration all connected in one system.
features: User authentication: signup and login with JWT tokens, plus authentication middleware that checks the user on every protected route.
Author profiles: each creator has a profile record that is read and updated separately from the account record.
Article creation and management: creators write articles under categories, edit them, and manage published and draft posts from a dashboard.
AI-powered content moderation: submitted articles are reviewed by an AI step before being accepted.
Engagement tracking: separate models store likes, comments, shares and views for every article.
Creator earnings: earnings are computed from views using RPM groups, and a creator dashboard shows them.
Withdrawal requests: creators request payouts, which are saved as withdrawal records for admin review.
Admin analytics: counts of articles, likes, comments, shares and aggregated views.
Admin controls: user administration, category and RPM group setup, and earnings administration.
Database-backed content storage with MongoDB.
workflow: A visitor or administrator sends a request to the Express app in index.js.
The app mounts user routes (user.routes.js) and admin routes (host.routes.js).
Authentication middleware verifies the JWT and loads the user record before protected routes run.
Publishing routes load categories, create articles in the article model and list articles for readers.
When readers open an article, the view controller records a view, and likes, comments and shares are saved to their own models.
The creator dashboard reads articles, views, comments and shares and calculates earnings from RPM rules.
Creators submit withdrawal requests, which are stored and shown to the admin.
The admin dashboard aggregates all engagement data and manages users, categories, RPM groups and payouts.

modules.role: Express entry point that receives all requests and mounts user and admin routes.
Routes for authentication, profiles, publishing, dashboard and withdrawals.
Admin routes for analytics, users, setup, operations and earnings.
Account creation, login and user administration logic.
JWT verification that protects private routes.
User accounts and author profile data.
Articles and their categories.
Engagement records used for analytics and earnings.
Records views when an article is opened.
Revenue-per-thousand-views rules used to calculate earnings.
Stores creator payout requests.
Front-end pages for the creator dashboard, signup, blog reading and admin dashboard.

challenges: Modelling engagement so views, likes, comments and shares can be aggregated quickly for analytics.
Keeping creator earnings accurate when RPM rules change per category or group.
Protecting admin and creator routes so each role can only reach its own data.
futureImprovements: Add payment gateway integration for real payouts.
Add full-text search and tag filtering.
Add email notifications for approvals and withdrawals.
Cache analytics queries to speed up the admin dashboard.

name: Multi-Agent Orchestration System
projectType: Autonomous deep-research agent (plan, execute, evaluate loop)
description: The Multi-Agent Orchestration System is a command-line research assistant in which several specialized components cooperate to answer hard questions. Instead of asking a language model once, the system runs a loop. An action planner decides what to do next, a tool executor performs web searches and reads pages, a sufficiency evaluator judges whether enough evidence has been gathered, and a final-answer component writes the result. A shared pipeline state object carries the question, gathered results and decisions between stages, and every model call goes through one LLM client with a JSON parser to turn replies into structured data.
features: Action planner that reads shared state and chooses the next research step.
Tool executor that dispatches Tavily web searches and page-research calls.
Sufficiency evaluator that decides when the evidence is good enough to stop.
Final-answer stage that formats the approved result for the user.
Shared pipeline state updated by every stage of the loop.
JSON parser that converts model replies into structured decisions.
In-memory buffer for short-term memory.
Single LLM client wrapping the chat model API.
Simple CLI entry point (main.py).
workflow: The user submits a request in the CLI (main.py), which creates the pipeline state and starts the workflow.
The research loop asks the planner for the next action based on the current state.
The planner calls the LLM client and parses the JSON reply into an action.
The executor runs the action: Tavily web search, or fetching and reading web pages.
Results are written into the pipeline state.
The evaluator asks the LLM whether the evidence is sufficient and parses the verdict.
If insufficient, the loop returns to planning; if sufficient, the final-answer module formats the response.
The answer is printed to the user.

modules.role: CLI entry point that accepts the request, creates state and starts the workflow.
Research loop that coordinates planning, execution, evaluation and final answer.
Action planner that reads state and requests the next step from the LLM.
Tool executor that dispatches searches and page research.
Sufficiency evaluator that decides whether to stop or continue.
Formats the approved result into the final response.
Pipeline state shared by all stages.
Web search (Tavily) and page research tools.
LLM client that sends chat requests to the model API.
In-memory buffer for short-term context.

challenges: Preventing the loop from running forever when evidence is never judged sufficient.
Getting the LLM to return strictly parseable JSON for planning and evaluation.
Keeping shared state small enough to fit within the model context.
futureImprovements: Add a maximum iteration and cost limit.
Add source citations to the final answer.
Persist state to disk so research can resume.

name: ChatMind
description: ChatMind is a ChatGPT-style web application where signed-in users hold conversations with an AI assistant and keep their history. The interface is a Next.js home screen composed of a sidebar with history, new chat, search, projects, share popup, profile menu, a more-options menu, a message display area and a message input. Behind it, API routes handle chat, saving the assistant's reply, history queries, signup, login, token refresh and token verification. Users, chats and messages are stored in a database, signup sends a welcome email, and an AI helper module generates the replies.
features: Secure signup and login with generated access and refresh tokens.
Token refresh API so sessions continue without logging in again.
Welcome email on signup through a mail helper.
Chat API that stores the user message, requests an AI reply and persists it.
Persistent chat history shown in the sidebar and a history view.
Search through conversations.
Projects view for organizing chats.
Share popup, profile view and more-options menu.
Message display and message input components.
Shared database connector for users, chats and messages.
workflow: The user opens the Next.js home screen (page.tsx), which renders the sidebar, search, projects, profile, message display and message input.
On signup, the Signup API creates the user record and sends an email through the mail helper.
On login, the Login API checks the user and generates tokens; the Token refresh API issues new ones later.
When the user sends a prompt, the Chat API verifies the token through the verification module.
The Chat API reads or creates the chat, stores the user message and asks the AI helper for a reply.
The assistant reply is submitted to the Save assistant reply route and stored in message records.
The sidebar and history view call the History API, which queries stored chats.

modules.role: Home screen plus message display and message input.

modules.role: Persist replies and query history.

Token verification, token generation and signup email.
Database connector.
User, chat and message data models.

challenges: Keeping sessions secure while avoiding repeated logins, which needed access and refresh tokens.
Storing user and assistant messages consistently within the right chat.
Rendering long histories quickly in the sidebar.
futureImprovements: Stream AI replies token by token.
Add rate limiting and usage quotas.

name: LawMemory Bot
description: LawMemory Bot is a small terminal chatbot built on the Gemini model that remembers the whole conversation. A system prompt, defined in its own file, sets the assistant's role, which the repository name suggests is a legal-information assistant. That prompt seeds a message history; every question and answer is appended to it, and the complete history is sent to the model on each turn so follow-up questions make sense.
features: System prompt that defines the assistant's role and behavior.
Message history seeded with the system prompt.
Every turn appended so context is preserved.
Gemini model configured in a separate setup file.
Interactive terminal chat loop.
workflow: The user starts the program and enters a question.
The chat loop builds the system prompt from memorySystem.py.
The prompt seeds the message history.
The loop gets the Gemini model from the model setup file.
The user message is appended and the model is invoked with the full history.
The reply is returned, appended to history and printed, ready for the next question.

modules.role: Chat loop and message history.
System prompt that seeds the history.
Model setup that configures Gemini.

challenges: History grows with every turn and can exceed the model's context limit.
The assistant must not present answers as professional legal advice.
futureImprovements: Persist history to disk between sessions.

name: PDF Chat (Chroma RAG v2)
description: PDF Chat v2 lets a user ask questions about a PDF and receive answers grounded in its content. It has two parts. An indexing script loads the PDF, splits it into chunks, embeds them and persists the vectors into a Chroma index. An interactive assistant takes a question, embeds it, retrieves the most relevant passages from Chroma, builds a context prompt and asks Google Gemini to answer using that context.
features: PDF page loading.
Text splitting into overlapping chunks.
Embedding and persistent Chroma vector storage.
Query embedding and passage retrieval.
Context prompt that combines question and passages.
Gemini answers grounded in the retrieved text.
Interactive command-line assistant.
workflow: createDB.py loads the source PDF pages.
The pages are split into chunks.
The chunks are embedded and the vectors persisted to the Chroma index.
The user asks a question in main.py.
The question is embedded and Chroma is searched for similar passages.
A context prompt is built from the question and passages.
Gemini is invoked and the response is printed.

modules.role: PDF indexing: load, split, embed and persist.
Interactive assistant, retrieval, prompt building and Gemini call.

challenges: Choosing chunk sizes that keep meaning without wasting context.
Ensuring answers come only from retrieved passages.
futureImprovements: Support multiple PDFs and other file types.

name: SDK Tool-Calling Research Agent
description: This project is a research agent written directly against an OpenAI-compatible SDK, without an agent framework. It implements its own agent loop, tool registry, tool schemas and conversation memory, which exposes how native function calling works. The agent can search the web with DuckDuckGo and fetch and extract text from source pages.

Tool registry and schema module.
DuckDuckGo web search tool.
Source research tool with page extraction.
Conversation memory used by every component.
OpenAI-compatible model client.
CLI launcher and conversation loop.
workflow: main.py starts the conversation loop in enterpoint.py.
The user's question is recorded in conversation memory.
The loop calls run_Agent.py.
The model client reads history and gets tool definitions from too_schema.py and TOOL_REGISTRY.py.
The completion request goes to the OpenAI-compatible API.
If a tool is requested, search or source research runs and results are written to memory.
The loop repeats until the model returns a final answer.

name: ArticleForge
description: ArticleForge turns a single topic into a finished article through four stages that each do one job. An outline creator structures the piece, a content analyzer checks drafts, an article writer produces the text and an article editor polishes it. Each stage builds its prompt from a shared prompt-template module and sends it through one LLM client to a configured API.

The final article is returned and printed.

name: ToolMate
description: ToolMate is a question-answering agent that decides when to use tools. It has three: a DuckDuckGo web search tool, a webpage reader and a calculator. A model factory configures a chat model that calls OpenRouter, the agent streams the completion to the user, and an answer formatter prepares the final output.
